items.headline: Great American AI Act discussion draft proposes a three-year federal preemption of state frontier-AI rules
items.diff_narrative: This is a fresh policy story with no antecedent in yesterday's brief, which centered on product and market news (Microsoft Scout, Nemotron 3 Ultra, Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, SpaceX IPO). The new item moves coverage into federal AI governance: Reps. Obernolte and Trahan released a roughly 270-page bipartisan discussion draft whose headline provision would preempt for three years any state law that specifically regulates the development of frontier models - taking aim at California's AB 2013 and part of SB 942 - while preserving state laws of general applicability and rules on AI use or deployment. In exchange the draft builds a federal layer, requiring developers above a reported $500M prior-year revenue threshold to publish a public frontier-AI framework for catastrophic-risk management and codifying the Commerce Department's Center for AI Standards and Innovation with $100M a year for FY2027-2029. Reaction split immediately along the preemption line, setting up the central fight as the text moves toward a real bill.

items.headline: Langroid CVE-2026-25879 prompt-to-SQL RCE keeps the agentic SQL attack surface in the spotlight
items.diff_narrative: Security was absent from yesterday's slate, so this critical-vulnerability story is entirely new. A fresh advisory rates CVE-2026-25879 in Langroid's SQLChatAgent at CVSS 9.8: because the agent executes model-authored SQL that prompt injection can steer, an attacker can reach dangerous dialect-specific primitives (PostgreSQL pg_execute_server_program, MySQL FILE, MSSQL xp_cmdshell) and escalate from data theft to remote code execution on the database host when the agent runs under an over-privileged role; the fix in Langroid 0.63.0 defaults to a sqlglot-parsed SELECT-only allowlist plus a dangerous-pattern blocklist. The item explicitly ties this to the actively exploited LiteLLM proxy injection (CVE-2026-42208), framing both as the same text-to-SQL-to-database pattern and drawing the lesson that any LLM allowed to write SQL must run against a least-privilege, read-only-by-default role. This connects to the brief's recurring open-agent-harness thread from a defensive angle rather than the product angle of prior days.

items.headline: MiniMax M3 open-weight 1M-context coding model claims to beat GPT-5.5 on SWE-Bench Pro - but weights are not out yet
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's open-weights story was Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B, whose weights had actually shipped to Hugging Face; today's open-weights entry is a different and more conditional one. China's MiniMax launched M3, billed as the first open-weight model combining frontier coding-agent performance, a one-million-token context window, and native multimodality, built on a new MiniMax Sparse Attention mechanism and reportedly trained on roughly 100 trillion interleaved text-image tokens at about a twentieth of M2.7's per-token compute. MiniMax reports 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro - ahead of GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, approaching Claude Opus 4.7 - and 83.5 on BrowseComp. The key contrast with the Nemotron item is verifiability: M3's scores are company-reported on its own infrastructure, the model is reachable only via the MiniMax API and Code agent app, and the promised weights and technical report have not yet appeared on the MiniMaxAI Hugging Face org (still showing M2.7 as its newest checkpoint), so M3 is a benchmark claim to watch rather than something a team can self-host today.

items.headline: Bay Area June-July events to plan attendance around
items.diff_narrative: The events round-up carries forward from yesterday with the calendar advanced one step. Microsoft Build and Snowflake Summit, which yesterday were noted as just-wrapped, are now dropped entirely as closed, and Apple WWDC26 (June 8-12 at Apple Park) becomes the next still-upcoming event, with today's entry adding granular detail - the keynote at 10:00 AM PT and Platforms State of the Union at 1:00 PM PT on Monday June 8, followed by 100-plus video sessions and Group Labs. The remaining lineup holds steady: Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18 at Moscone), now described with its keynote roster (Ghodsi, Zaharia, Nadella by recorded fireside, OpenAI's Greg Brockman) and an OpenAI-partnered hackathon; the AI Engineer World's Fair (Day 0 June 28, main program June 29-July 2); AI Tinkerers SF meetups; and the further-out GitHub Universe (Oct 28-29) and AWS re:Invent (Nov 30-Dec 4, registration opening June 16).
